\section[el juicio]{el juicio — the trial; judgement}

\label{lesson:ES-C522-juicio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to find out, then the Spanish for to suspect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el juicio}
\textbf{el juicio} — \textquotedblleft{}the trial; judgement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El juicio empieza el martes.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The trial starts on Tuesday.}
\end{quote}

\emph{A mi juicio} — in my judgement.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{juicio} is inherited from Latin \emph{iūdicium} 'a trial, a judgement' (EtymDB), built on \emph{iūdex} 'a judge'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el juicio}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el juicio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el juicio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to find out, then the Spanish for to suspect, then say \emph{el juicio} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el juicio mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The trial; judgement\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el juez]{el juez — the judge}

\label{lesson:ES-C522-juez}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to suspect, then the Spanish for the trial.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el juez}
\textbf{el juez} — \textquotedblleft{}the judge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El juez escuchó a los testigos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The judge listened to the witnesses.}
\end{quote}

A woman judge is \emph{la jueza} or \emph{la juez}. Plural: \emph{los jueces}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{juez} is inherited from Latin \emph{iūdex} 'a judge' (EtymDB), built on \emph{iūs} 'law' and \emph{dīcere} 'to say'. The judge is the one who says what the law is.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el juez}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el juez}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el juez}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to suspect, then the Spanish for the trial, then say \emph{el juez} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el juez mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The judge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[juzgar]{juzgar — to judge, to try}

\label{lesson:ES-C522-juzgar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the trial, then the Spanish for the judge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: juzgar}
\textbf{juzgar} — \textquotedblleft{}to judge, to try\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Lo juzgaron por robo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{They tried him for robbery.}
\end{quote}

It takes \emph{gu} before \emph{e}: \emph{juzgué}. Also everyday: \emph{No me juzgues.}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{juzgar} is inherited from Latin \emph{iūdicāre} 'to judge', through old Spanish \emph{judgar} (EtymDB). It is built on \emph{iūdex} 'a judge'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{juzgar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{juzgar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{juzgar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the trial, then the Spanish for the judge, then say \emph{juzgar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does juzgar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To judge, to try\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[condenar]{condenar — to sentence, to condemn}

\label{lesson:ES-C522-condenar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the judge, then the Spanish for to judge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: condenar}
\textbf{condenar} — \textquotedblleft{}to sentence, to condemn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Lo condenaron a pagar una multa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He was sentenced to pay a fine.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Condenar a alguien a...} — to sentence someone to...

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{condenar} is inherited from Latin \emph{condemnāre} 'to sentence, to condemn' (EtymDB), built on \emph{con-} and \emph{damnāre} 'to condemn'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{condenar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{condenar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the judge, then the Spanish for to judge, then say \emph{condenar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la cárcel]{la cárcel — the prison, the jail}

\label{lesson:ES-C522-carcel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to judge, then the Spanish for to sentence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la cárcel}
\textbf{la cárcel} — \textquotedblleft{}the prison, the jail\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pasó tres años en la cárcel.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He spent three years in prison.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La prisión} is a more formal word.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{cárcel} is inherited from Latin \emph{carcer} 'a prison, an enclosure', through old Spanish \emph{carcel} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la cárcel}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la cárcel}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la cárcel}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to judge, then the Spanish for to sentence, then say \emph{la cárcel} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
